findings.title: Reassigning exit code 4 breaks existing automation
findings.body: This changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and reuses 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED. The exit codes are the documented programmatic contract of update-compatibility, so scripts built against the previous release will now treat a recreate result (3) differently and will interpret 4 as feature-disabled rather than recreate-required. Even for a preview tool, this is a breaking contract change; preserving 4 for recreate and allocating a new code for FEATURE_DISABLED would avoid the break.

findings.title: New exit-code paths are not asserted
findings.body: The new feature-disabled path returns CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), and the recreate path now returns 3, but the tests only assert stderr text. testFeatureNotEnabled asserts the error message and testWrongVersions asserts the incompatibility message, but neither checks the process exit code. A bug in picocli.exit or a future change to the constants could silently break the documented exit-code contract. Add assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode()) to testFeatureNotEnabled and assertEquals(3, result.exitCode()) to testWrongVersions.

findings.title: Warning overstates when the rolling-updates feature is required
findings.body: The caution says the Operator will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled, but the PR's own UpgradeTest runs the default strategy case (`spec.update` not set) without enabling the feature and expects deployments and upgrades to work. The feature is only required when `spec.update` is configured. Scope the warning to that case so users do not believe an existing CR must enable a preview feature just to keep the operator running.
